title.en: Static and non-visual fallback for a spatial result

summary: Deliver the finding of a spatial scene in a form that survives without three-dimensional rendering, colour perception or pointer input.
objective: A reader who never sees the interactive scene can still obtain its finding, and every conclusion the scene supports appears in the fallback.
intent_signals: what if webgl is not available
describe the scene for a screen reader
include a static version in the report
the viewer only has a keyboard
example_prompts: Add a static summary of an interactive scene for a written report.
Provide a keyboard and text route to the same conclusion.
Make the finding survive being printed in black and white.
not_for: Artifacts with no stated finding, where there is nothing to carry over.
Purely decorative motion that makes no claim.

principles: The fallback carries the finding, not the scene. Describing camera moves and colours is not a substitute for stating what the scene shows.

A three-dimensional view can fail for many reasons: no graphics context, a lost context, reduced-motion preferences, no pointer, no colour discrimination, or a printed page. One fallback can address all of them if it is built around the conclusion.

Non-text content needs a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose. That is an equivalence requirement, not a caption requirement, and it is what makes the fallback substantive rather than decorative.
Colour must not be the only carrier of a distinction. Shape, position, label, ordering and pattern all remain available, and a scene that relies on hue alone loses its meaning in the fallback.
Visual information needed to identify a control or a graphical object needs sufficient contrast against what is next to it, which constrains legends, outlines and state indicators in the static view.
Numbers beat descriptions of numbers. Where the scene shows quantities, the fallback should carry the quantities themselves in a readable table rather than an adjective.
The fallback is a deliverable with its own correctness. It has to be updated when the scene changes, or it becomes a confident record of an older result.
implementation: Write the finding first as a short statement, then build the fallback around supporting it: one or more static frames from named viewpoints, a text description, and a table of the values the scene displays.
Choose the static viewpoints deliberately so that together they show what a viewer would have obtained by orbiting, and label each with what it is meant to establish.
Give every visual distinction a second, non-colour carrier such as a label, a pattern, an ordering or a position, and confirm the distinctions survive a greyscale rendering.
Keep legends, outlines and state markers distinguishable against their surroundings, and check them at the contrast level the guidance requires rather than by eye alone.
Provide the underlying values in a readable structure alongside the images, and include units and the value range.

Offer a non-pointer route to the same states: named viewpoint buttons, a list of selectable parts and keyboard-reachable controls, so that spatial actions have an equivalent that does not require dragging.
Detect the absence of a working three-dimensional context and present the fallback instead of an empty area or an error.
Regenerate the fallback whenever the scene changes, and record which scene revision it corresponds to.
observable_checks: A reader given only the fallback can state the scene's finding correctly.
The fallback rendered in greyscale still distinguishes every category the scene distinguishes.
Every quantity displayed in the scene appears in the fallback with its units.
Each spatial action offered in the scene has a named, keyboard-reachable equivalent that reaches the same state.
With the three-dimensional context unavailable, the fallback appears in place of an empty area or a raw error.
The fallback names the scene revision it was generated from, and that revision matches the current scene.

creative_affordances: The fallback can be a designed artifact in its own right, such as a plate of annotated views, rather than an apologetic reduction.
Chosen viewpoints and annotations are an editorial opportunity to state the finding more directly than free exploration does.
known_limits: Meeting the criteria cited here for a fallback does not make the interactive scene itself conformant; that requires its own evaluation.
No conformance evaluation, assistive-technology test or contrast measurement was performed for this record.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact has been executed or observed for this record.

claims.statement: WCAG 2.2 requires at Level A that all non-text content presented to the user have a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose apart from listed exceptions, requires at Level A that colour not be used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response or distinguishing a visual element, and requires at Level AA a contrast ratio of at least three to one against adjacent colours for the visual information needed to identify user interface components and their states.
claims.scope: Normative success criteria of the W3C Recommendation of 12 December 2024, read on the access date. They state requirements; no conformance evaluation was performed for this record.
